A.a: Labor - how much the factory has to pay its workers.
Agglomeration, when companies cluster together so they can share services and workers.
The cost of shipping the raw materials to the factory and the products to the market.

B.a: T1- Copper ore is mostly waste rock, so the finished copper weighs way less. E2- Smelters near the mines remove that rock. A3- That way they only ship the light copper, which saves on transportation costs.
The final product is lighter than the raw ore, so it's cheaper to process it near the mine and ship the smaller amount.
Because the raw material loses a lot of weight during processing, it would be a waste of money to transport all that heavy ore to a factory far away.
Smelting removes most of the weight, so locating near the mine cuts shipping costs.
Copper smelters are built near copper mines because that is where the copper is.
Bulk-reducing industries locate near the market because the finished product weighs more and is expensive to ship.
The copper loses most of its weight when it gets processed.
They locate near the raw materials because workers in mining towns are cheaper, so they save on labor costs.

C.a: T1- Britain had a lot of coal and iron. E2- Coal powered the steam engines and iron was used to build machines. A3- So factories could be built quickly.
Britain had colonies that gave it raw materials like cotton and places to sell goods, which made factory owners lots of money to build even more factories.
Lots of rivers and canals made it cheap to move coal and goods around the country.
The Agricultural Revolution meant fewer farm workers were needed, so lots of people moved to cities and became workers in the new factories.
The Industrial Revolution started in Britain because Britain was rich and powerful.
Britain had lots of oil, which they used to power the first factories.
Britain had large deposits of coal and iron ore.
Britain was the first country to have electricity, which ran all the machines in the factories.

D.a: T1- Automation. E2- Robots in car factories can do the jobs of many workers. A3- So companies needed fewer workers and laid people off.
Companies moved factories to Mexico and China where they can pay workers less, so Rust Belt plants closed.
Japanese car companies made cheaper, better cars in the 1970s and 80s, so American automakers lost sales and cut jobs in Detroit.
Outsourcing to countries with lower wages made it cheaper to produce there, so factories in Ohio shut down.
The factories got old and rusty.
The Rust Belt deindustrialized because the Industrial Revolution created too many factories.
Factories closed because workers moved to the Sun Belt for the warm weather, so there was nobody left to work in them.

E.a: T1- Detroit lost a lot of people. E2- When the car factories closed, workers lost their jobs and moved away, and the population fell from almost 2 million to about 640,000. A3- That shrank the tax base, so the city went bankrupt.
In Cleveland, when the steel mills shut down lots of people became unemployed, which led to poverty in those neighborhoods.
Pittsburgh lost its steel jobs, so it shifted to a service economy based on hospitals, universities, and tech.
Youngstown, Ohio lost thousands of steel jobs when the mills closed, so people left and lots of houses were abandoned.
Deindustrialization had a big effect on the city and made it worse.
Detroit grew a lot because new factories opened there in the 2000s.
Detroit's population went down a lot.
Houston lost jobs when its oil factories closed, so people moved away.

F.a: T1- Microloans are small loans for poor people who can't get bank loans. E2- In Bangladesh, Grameen Bank lends to women who buy things like sewing machines to start businesses. A3- The money they earn helps pay for their kids' school and food.
Women can borrow a little money to start a small business, like selling vegetables, and then they earn their own income and get more say in their family.
Microloans let women who don't have collateral start their own small businesses, which raises the family's income and helps the kids stay healthy.
They give tiny loans so women can buy a cow or a phone and make money, which lifts their families out of poverty.
Microloans are large loans from the World Bank to build dams and factories in developing countries.
Microloans are small loans to poor women so they can start a business.
Microloans are free money from the government that women don't have to pay back, so they can buy food for their families.

G.a: T1- Ecotourism brings in money from tourists who come to see nature. E2- In Costa Rica, tourists pay to visit rainforests and locals get jobs as guides. A3- This gives people a reason to protect the forest instead of cutting it down. One drawback is that too many tourists can damage the habitat.
Tourists pay to see gorillas in Rwanda, which creates jobs, so people want to keep the gorillas safe for the future. But flying there causes a lot of pollution.

Ecotourism creates jobs for local people, and because the forest is worth more standing than cut down, communities conserve it. A drawback is that a lot of the profits go to foreign hotel companies instead of locals.
Visitors spend money at eco-lodges, which gives locals income, and that makes them want to protect the animals. However, crowds of tourists can disturb wildlife and cause erosion on the trails.
Ecotourism is good because people like to see animals.
Ecotourism supports sustainable development because it builds big resorts and factories in the rainforest, but it is expensive.
Ecotourism brings in money and jobs from tourists, which gives locals a reason to protect nature.
Ecotourism helps because tourists volunteer to plant trees for free, so the country doesn't have to pay for it. A drawback is that tourists might get bored.
